decisions: Commands use typed ids (CustomerId, ApproverId); registrations return Guid, status changes return CustomerId/ApproverId. Callers (API, bulk) build ids via CustomerId.Create(guid).
DTOs expose Guid ids, string fields and domain status enums, so the infrastructure query projections stay simple and serialize cleanly.
Validators and handlers are discovered by assembly scanning; CustomerRuleBuilderExtensions is internal. Handlers are named *Handler, not *CommandHandler.
ChangeWorkshopStatus/GetWorkshopDetail take typed WorkshopId (like Maintenance VehicleId); the API must build it with WorkshopId.Create(guid). Register returns Guid; status change returns WorkshopId.
DTOs expose Guid ids (not WorkshopId) so System.Text.Json serializes them plainly; Status is the WorkshopStatus enum.
Application namespace for commands/queries/DTOs/handlers is RutaViva.Workshops.Application.Workshops (handlers of queries in .Queries); no DI registration file was created (not in my list).
IFleetReferenceWriter has UpsertCustomerAsync/UpsertWorkshopAsync/UpsertApproverAsync(reference, ct); Infrastructure must add-or-update by Id (works for new and tracked/untracked entities).
Unknown replicated status string yields ReferenceErrors.InvalidStatus (Application, Validation) because the Fleet domain catalog has no such error; Registered handlers fail without upsert.
StatusChanged for an unknown entity logs ReferenceUpdateIgnored (Warning) and returns success without upsert or SaveChanges.
Commands use strong ids (CustomerId, WorkshopId, ApproverId?, VehicleId) like Maintenance; API/bulk must build them from Guid via Create. RegisterVehicleHandler returns Guid.
VehicleErrors has no vehicle-not-found: added VehicleApplicationErrors.NotFound (Vehicle.NotFound, ErrorType.NotFound) and InvalidStatus in Fleet.Application.Vehicles; API maps it to 404.
RegisterVehicleCommandValidator takes IClock (year range depends on current year); a blank Vin is treated as no VIN. Ports sit directly in the Vehicles namespace.
